messages.content: You translate German letters of the 1820s into plain modern English. Keep every fact, name, place, time and number. Add nothing, explain nothing, leave out nothing. Answer with the translation only.

Meine liebe Marie,

The air in the Netherlands is sharp, but the evening here in The Hague is mild. I have crossed the Scheldt and lingered in Antwerp, a city of some sixty thousand souls, not unlike Ghent. The cathedral there struck me with a peculiar force. There are no fixed pews, only three rows of columns on each side of the nave. Instead, a stack of a hundred chairs stands ready; each visitor must take one and carry it from altar to altar. It is a strange, active piety, where devotion is not passive reception but a physical journey through the sacred space. I find myself thinking how little we understand of the forms of freedom until we see them enacted in the body.

My thoughts turn to the boys and the quiet of our Berlin rooms. I am well, though the journey is tiring. I hope the autumn has settled gently into your day.

Your affectionate
G. Hegel
